summary: Iteration 1 fully confirmed both hypotheses: the two-phase adaptive search finds a complete Pareto front (62–80 non-dominated configs across all 8 GPU tiers) in just 200 evaluations (~18 seconds wall time), and KV block capacity shows a clean saturating threshold effect on TTFT p99. The configuration space has surprisingly low effective dimensionality — GPU count dominates throughput, while KV blocks and max-running-reqs each have simple binary threshold behavior.
key_points: Search algorithm validated: 200 evaluations (11.1% of 1800 configs) found 62–80 Pareto-optimal configurations covering all GPU tiers (1–8 GPUs), far exceeding the predicted minimum of 20. Best config: tp=8, i=1 at 32.0 rps with 27.5ms TTFT p99.

KV block dose-response confirmed exactly: TTFT p99 drops from 9,252ms → 4,776ms → 2,682ms → 39ms as blocks increase from 2,000 to 5,000, then plateaus perfectly at 39ms through 10,000 blocks — the threshold for zero preemptions falls between 4,000–5,000 blocks at tp=2, i=2, rate=100.

Still unknown: how the KV block threshold and Pareto front structure shift at different request rates (e.g., rate=50 or rate=200). Next iteration should test search.py robustness across rates and explore whether the preemption threshold can be predicted analytically from workload parameters (rate × mean request length).
